rep.angle: lead with a peer company's result
rep.name: Rohan

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Priya, Rohan at HyperSale—a freight brokerage used AI roleplays to catch coaching gaps weekly instead of at quota time. Can I take four minutes?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: I’ve got two, not four. What exactly do you mean by “coaching gaps”?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Things like missed discovery questions, weak objection handling, or talking over buyers. Reps practice with realistic AI buyers, and every score cites the exact quote.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Mm-hm. Practice scores are one thing—how does that tell me which rep is actually coachable before they miss quota?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: The main thing is reps can practice anytime, while managers get weekly skill trends and quote-backed scores. Do you already run weekly coaching?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: We do ride-alongs. But you didn’t answer me—how do those trends distinguish a coachable rep from someone who’s just good at roleplay?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: The trendline shows whether scores improve week by week, and every score links to their exact language. Could we maybe schedule something?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Not yet. You’re still showing me who improves at roleplay, not whether that predicts who responds to coaching on real calls.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: It doesn’t prove that alone; in a pilot, managers compare roleplay trends with ride-along observations. Could we maybe set up a follow-up?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Maybe. We bought Gong and nobody used it, so why would my reps use this enough for a pilot to tell us anything?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Reps can practice in short, realistic sessions, and managers see weekly participation and improvement. Would you be open to a quick demo next week?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: No. Tracking participation doesn’t create adoption—what actually gets a freight broker to use this when Gong became shelfware?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Usually managers assign one five-minute freight objection before coaching, then review the quote-backed score together. Could we maybe reconnect sometime next week?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Mm. That’s more concrete. Send me 20 minutes next week, but show me the rep workflow and how we’d compare it with ride-along notes—not a generic demo.
